GOVQA – P002875-032421

Mr. Greenewald,


The New Mexico Department of Public Safety (DPS) recently received your Inspection of Public Records
request, pursuant to NMSA 14-2-1 et seq., regarding your request “the entire personnel file of New
Mexico State Police officer Sergeant Richard C. Doty. He began circa August of 1988 as a Staff
Sergeant, and January 1999 as a sergeant.”

- Some materials that may exist are being redacted pursuant to the Inspection of Public Records Act,
NMSA 14-2-1{A)(12), in which every person has a right to inspect public records of this state except:

"as otherwise provided by law,"

In conjunction with the above exception records related to your request that may exist
are being redacted pursuant to NMAC 1,7.1.12 EMPLOYMENT RECORDS: sub section C.

"For the purpose of inspection of public records under Subsection B of 1.7.1.12 NMAC, the following
material shall be regarded as confidential and exempted from public inspection: records and
documentation pertaining to physical or mental illness, injury or examinations, sick leave and medical
treatment of persons; records and documentation maintained for purposes of the Americans with
Disabilities Act [42 U.S.C. Section 12010 et seq]; letters of reference concerning employment, licensing,
or permits; records and documentation containing matters of opinion; documents concerning
infractions and disciplinary actions; performance appraisals; opinions as to whether a person should be
re-employed; college transcripts; military discharge; information on the race, color, religion, sex,
national origin, political affiliation, age, and disability of employees; home address and personal
telephone number unless related to public business; social security number; laboratory reports or test
results generated according to the provisions of 1.7.8 NMAC; and as otherwise provided by state or
federal law."

In addition, redactions on Computer Aided Dispatch documents were made due to the
fact that it is information provided by the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a
computerized index of documented criminal justice information housed by the Criminal Justice
Information Services (CJIS), a division of the Federal Bureau of Investigation
{FBI). The information indexed in NCIC is for law enforcement purposes only. This is in accordance with
Title 28, Code of Federal Regulations:
"Data in NCIC files are exchanged with and for the official use of criminal justice officials of local, state,
and federal governments in the United States and its possessions and in Canada".

Finally, - Specific identifiers have been redacted pursuant to New Mexico Inspection of
Public Records Act. NMSA 1978, Sections 14-2-1 {B) and 14-2-G{E) together allow
"protected personal identifier" information to be redacted as follow:

"(1) all but the last four digits of a: (a) taxpayer identification number; (b) financial
account number; or (c) driver's license number; (2) all but the year of a person's date of birth; and (3) a
social security number."

Some materials that may exist are being withheld pursuant to State, Ex rel. Newsome v. Alarid, 90 N.M
at 790; 1977-NMSC-076, which states:

"We hold that letter of references, documents concerning infractions and disciplinary action,
personnel evaluations, opinions as to whether a person would be re-hired or as to why an applicant
was not hired, and any other matters of opinions are also exempt from disclosure under the [IPRAJ
statute. Newsome, 1977-NMSC-076, ,112."

Please find the enclosed document responsive to your request.


Sincerely,


Regina Chacon
Records Custodian
Department of Public Safety

   DATE:     DECEMBER 14, 2005

  FROM:      CHIEF CARLOS R. MALDONADO
             DEPUTY SECRETARY - OPERATIONS

      TO:    SERGEANT RICHARD DOTY
             DPS/ NEW MEXICO STATE POLICE
             P.O. BOX 517
             GRANTS, NM 87020


SUBJECT:     FLEET ACCIDENT - CLASSIFICATION AND NOTIFICATION OF
             SUSPENSION     ___________ ____________________ ___

  On November 2, 2005, the Department of Public Safety Fleet Management, in
  conjunction with the Fleet Safety Committee, heard you appeal of your accident per your
  request. The results of the review are as follows:

  The appeal was for the fleet accident that you were involved in on March 24, 2004 in unit
  512-01, was classified as a chargeable “Class B” type, in accordance with Department of
  Public Safety Policies and Procedures, Policy ADM: 18:00.

  A “Class B” accident is defined as: The employee operated or parked a departmental
  vehicle in a manner that contributed to the cause of the vehicle being involved in an
  accident, even though the employee was not totally at fault or cited for a violation of the
  law.

  The fleet accident that you were involved in, on September 3, 2003, in unit 295-02, was
  classified as a chargeable “Class C” type, in accordance with Department of Public
  Safety Policies and Procedures, Policy ADM: 18:00.

 A “Class C” accident is defined as: The employee operated a departmental vehicle with
 obvious negligence, which was a direct cause of the accident.

 The above two fleet accidents were within a one-year period.

                                  B + C = 1 day suspension

 I am hereby providing you written notice of suspension from active duty, without pay, for
 the peiiod of one working day for the violation of Department of Public Safety Policies
 and Procedures, Policy ADM: 18:00.

 Your date(s) of suspension are as follows: December 20, 2005
Page 2
Intra-Dcpartmcntal Correspondence
Sergeant Rick Doty
December 14, 2005


I trust Sergeant Doty, that you will evaluate your driving procedures and remain alert at
all times when operating a motor vehicle. Your safety while operating departmental-
issued vehicles is of great concern. You must turn in all state-owned equipment to the
District Commander or his designee for the duration of your suspension.

hi the event you choose to appeal the classification decision, you may still appeal the
suspension pursuant to ADM: 18:00 and NMAC 5.100.8.43.2. If you choose to appeal
the suspension, you should notify me, in writing, within five (5) working days of your
receipt of this correspondence, if you desire a healing before a Disciplinary Hearing
Panel. Should you request a hearing before the Disciplinary Hearing Panel, the actions
described above will be held in abeyance and a Disciplinary Hearing Panel will be
convened.

   DATE:     APRIL 28,2005

  FROM:      CHIEF CARLOS R. MALDONADO
             DEPUTY SECRETARY - OPERATIONS

      TO:    SERGEANT RICHARD DOTY
             DPS/ NEW MEXICO STATE POLICE-NARC
             P.O. BOX 517
             GRANTS, NM 87020


SUBJECT:     FLEET ACCIDENT - CLASSIFICATION AND NOTIFICATION OF
             SUSPENSION

  On March 30, 2005, the Department of Public Safety Fleet Management, in conjunction
  with the Fleet Safety Committee, reviewed all fleet accidents for 2005. The results of the
  review are as follows:

  The fleet accident that you were involved in, on March 24, 2004, in unit 512-01, was
  classified as a chargeable “Class C” type, in accordance with Department of Public
  Safety Policies and Procedures, Policy ADM: 18:00.

  A “Class C” accident is defined as: The employee operated a departmental vehicle with
  obvious negligence, which was a direct cause of the accident.

  The above-identified chargeable accident is your second chargeable accident within a
  one-year period, with the first chargeable accident occurring on September 6, 2003. This
  accident was classified as a “Class C” type accident in accordance with Department of
  Public Safety Policies and Procedures, Policy ADM: 18:00.

  The above two accidents were within a one-year period.

                                  C + C = 2 day suspension

  I am hereby providing you written notice of suspension from active duty, without pay, for
  the period of one working day for the violation of Department of Public Safety Policies
  and Procedures, Policy ADM: 18:00.

  Your date(s) of suspension are as follows: May 9, 2005 and May 10 2005.

  I trust, Sergeant Doty, that you will evaluate your driving procedures and remain alert at
  all times when operating a motor vehicle. Your safety while operating departmental-
  issued vehicles is of great concern. You must turn in all state-owned equipment to the
  District Commander or his designee for the duration of your suspension.
                                                                                  Page 2
                                                      Intra-Departmental Correspondence
                                                                   Sergeant Richard Doty


Furthermore, pursuant to Department of Public Safety Policies and Procedures, ADM:
18:00, you are to notify me, in writing, within five (5) working days of receipt of this
correspondence, if you desire to appeal the classification decision. Should you appeal
this decision, the action described above will be held in abeyance until the next Fleet
Safety Committee can hear your appeal.

In the event you choose not to appeal the classification decision, you may still appeal the
suspension pursuant to ADM: 18:00 and NMAC 5.100.8.43.2. If you choose to appeal
the suspension, you should notify me, in writing, within five (5) working days of your
receipt of this correspondence, if you desire a hearing before a Disciplinary Hearing
Panel. Should you request a hearing before the Disciplinary Hearing Panel, the actions
described above will be held in abeyance and a Disciplinary Hearing Panel will be
convened.

SUBJECT:      FLEET ACCIDENT - CLASS “C” LETTER OF REPRIMAND


  The Department of Public Safety Fleet Safety Committee reviewed the circumstances
  surrounding your fleet accident which occurred on 09/06/03, involving Unit No. 0292-02.

  This accident was classified as a chargeable “Class C” type accident in accordance with
  Department of Public Safety Policies and Procedures.

  A “Class C” accident was defined as: The employee operated a departmental vehicle
  with obvious negligence which was a direct cause of the accident.

  This correspondence serves as an official notification of reprimand in accordance with
  Department of Public Safety Policies and Procedures, Policy ADM: 18:00.

  Your safe and efficient operation of departmental vehicles is of great concern to this
  office. You are reminded to remain alert to your operation of departmental vehicles and
  be aware of the actions of other motorists in order to reduce the probability of
  involvement in future accidents.

                              Acknowledgement and Consent Form

I have read the Executive Order, Executive Branch Information Technology Resources Policy
regarding Internet, Intranet, E-mail, and Digital Network Usage. I fully understand the terms of
this policy and agree to abide by them. I realize that the Department of Public Safety security
software may record for management use the Internet address of any site that I visit and keep a
record of any network activity in which I transmit or receive any kind of file. I know that any
violation of this policy could lead to dismissal or criminal prosecution.

I understand that the Department of Public Safety electronic mail system is Department of
Public Safety and State property and intended to be used primarily for business purposes. I
understand that excessive use of the E-mail system for the conduct of personal business is
strictly prohibited. I acknowledge that any message I send or receive may be recorded and
stored in an archive for management use.

I understand that Department of Public Safety reserves the right to access, review, and disclose
information obtained through the E-mail system at any time, with or without advance notice to
me and with or without my consent. I know that any violation of this policy could lead to
dismissal or criminal prosecution.

I confirm that I have read this employee acknowledgement and have had an opportunity ask
questions about it. I also agree to abide by the terms of the Information Technology Resource
Policy in this regard, a copy of which has been provided to me.

Re: FY07 Law Enforcement Program Pay Increases

We are pleased to inform you that effective July 15, 2006, you will receive a salary increase in accordance with the
FY07 Law Enforcement Officer Compensation Plan. Your new hourly salary will be $28,466, and the increase will
be reflected on the paycheck dated August 4, 2006. This salary represents placement at the appropriate step in
your rank based upon the total number of years in your current rank as of July 1, 2006.

If eligible (based upon performance and step), you will also receive a step increase beginning the pay period
following your class anniversary date. Officers with an anniversary date between 07/01/06 and 07/14/06 will
receive both the initial FY07 increase and their anniversary date-based step movement on July 15, 2006. Again,
the increase will be reflected on the paycheck dated August 4, 2006. Officers whose salary is at the highest step
for the rank will receive a lump sum payment equal to 3% of their annual salary in lieu of a step increase.

Prior to implementation of these increases, the Department’s pay policies will be updated to reflect the provisions of
the Law Enforcement Officer Compensation Plan for FY07.

Please note that this notice is based upon the most current data available to us. Though not expected, should
errors be found in the information a correction may be made.

We are pleased to be able to provide this salary increase, which resulted from the strong support law enforcement
received from Governor Bill Richardson and the New Mexico Legislature. Thank you for your continued service to
the Department of Public Safety and to the citizens of New Mexico.

Sincerely,


/s/

John Denko, Jr.
Cabinet Secretary

                   SUBJECT:       SPECIAL ASSIGNMENT
                                  RE: Annual Balloon Fiesta, Albuquerque, NM                     3
                                  Dates: October 5-13,2002


You are hereby assigned to assist with security and crowd control at the upcoming Balloon Fiesta
scheduled for October 5-13, 2002, in Albuquerque. You are directed to report to Lieutenant Mark
McCracken at the Albuquerque/District 05 office at 2:00 PM on Friday, October 4th, for orientation and
briefing. You will be released at 12:00 Noon on Sunday, October 13th, for return to you respective
district.

Per Diem is authorized at the rate of $65.00 per day. Ton are directed to take two (2)-regular days
offprior to reporting for this assignment When preparing your travel voucher, you are to utilize
your respective district cost center number. If you wish to submit for advanced Per Diem, you
must do so immediately in order to receive it before your report date, (Sign the travel voucher
in BLUE ink, and submit a new W-4 Form with it if you have not claimed Per Diem during the
last 6 months.) Arrangements have been made for lodging accommodations at the Amberley Suites
located at 7620 Pan American Freeway, NE, Albuquerque; telephone (505) 823-1300. The law
enforcement discount special rate is $69.00 + tax, single or double occupancy. Be sure to speak with
Agnes Martinez at the Amberley Suites, as she is handling the special rate for the State Police. You are
directed to contact the hotel to confirm your reservation and guarantee it with a credit card as
soon as you receive these orders, because if you delay, the hotel will not hold the rooms for us.

Attire will consist of the Class A uniform. You are to bring your cold weather jacket(s) and rain gear,
along with all regularly issued equipment.

I am confident that you will represent the New Mexico State Police, Department of Public Safety, in a
most exemplary manner. If, for some unforeseen reason, you are unable to comply with this assignment,
please contact your respective Zone Commander immediately at 827-9211,

  SUBJECT:       SPECIAL ASSIGNMENT
                     Re: NM Emergency Response to Radiation Terrorism Course
                          Nevada Test Site


Each of you is hereby assigned/approved to attend a training event at the Nevada Test Site the
week of September 22nd, 2002. The NM National Guard’s 64th Civil Support Team and the NM
Department of Public Safety are sponsoring this event.

The training will be based on responding to Radiation and Nuclear terrorist incidents and will
include classroom and hands-on training. Several first responders from around the state of NM
have been invited to come and participate. Your point of contact for this training is Paul E.
Nelson and he can be reached at (505) 980-2431.

For the week of September 22-28, 2002, attendees will be staying at the Nevada Test Site and at
the Excalibur Hotel & Casino in Las Vegas, Nevada. All travel and course fees have been paid.
In the event further reimbursement is required, it will have to be approved and processed by Mr.
Paul E. Nelson.

Included with your orders are several forms and documents indicating the plan of events and
training outlines. If for some reason, you are unable to comply with this assignment, you are to
contact Captain Juan P. Ontiveros immediately.

SUBJECT: NEW MEXICO EMERGENCY RESPONSE TO RADIATION TERRORISM
COURSE AT THE NEVADA TEST SITE


On behalf of the New Mexico National Guard's 64th Civil Support Team, I am inviting you to
send 4 emergency response officers and 2 bomb squad members to a training event at the
Nevada Test Site the week of September 22nd, 2002. This event is being sponsored by the
New Mexico National Guard’s 64™ Civil Support Team and the State of New Mexico -
Department of Public Safety.

The training will be based upon responding to Radiation and Nuclear terrorist incidents and
will include classroom and hands-on training events. Due to the hands-on portion of this
training, we are requesting participants be trained to the First Responder Operations level
(although Hazmat Technician/Specialist is preferred), in accordance with 29 CFR1910.120
(q) (6). There will be requirements for wearing of Level A and B equipment (Totally
Encapsulated Protective Clothing and/ or Self Contained Breathing Apparatus) so the
Department of Justice Medical Surveillance form will be required prior to attendance. This
will be sent in a couple of weeks.

For the week of September 22-28,2002, attendees will be staying at the Nevada Test Site
and in Las Vegas. All travel and course fees have been paid, therefore, there will be no cost
to your organization (other than salaries for your personnel) for the entire week. Fifty (50)
first responders from around the state of NM have been invited to come and participate. In
addition to the 64th CST, the 61st CST from Arkansas will also be attending and
participating. The training events will be based upon classroom training, as well as several
actual response scenarios where the entire incident command structure and varying levels
of emergency management will be participating.

Included in this packet are several forms and documents indicating the plan of events and
training outlines. These include a letter from Lt. Col. Michael Schwartz describing the
training event, an agenda of daily activities, training participation form for Department’s
Training officer to fill out, document describing all travel plans, State of NM reimbursement
form and attendee information sheet. Please provide me with the names of participants
from your organization no later than July 19,2002. All required forms should be sent to the
address above no later than September 13,2002,
Thank you in advance for helping to make this training event a success. I look forward to
working with you and your department’s attendees.


Paul E. Nelson, MS
Emergency Preparedness Specialists

                      CHIEF FRANK R. TAYLOR              V
FROM:
                      DPS/DEPUTY SECRETARY

TO:                   ALL BOMB TEAM MEMBERS

SUBJECT:              ASSIGNMENT-EOD TEAM IN-SERVICE SCHOOL


You are hereby assigned to attend the Explosive Ordinance Disposal Team In-Service
offered by the Department of Public Safety, from November 12, 2001 through November
16, 2001 in Las Cruces, New Mexico. You will report to Sergeant Richard Doty no later
than 0900 hours on November 12, 2001 at the Las Cruces State Police Office.

Per Diem is authorized for this assignment. Your completed per diem must utilize cost
center 0421800. All per diem requests are to be forwarded to Sergeant Richard Doty.

All personnel are to bring all assigned team equipment with them to this
assignment, to include at least two inert improvised explosive devices.

If you have any further questions, please contact Sergeant Richard Doty at 827-9322.

             SUBJECT:       SPECIAL ASSIGNMENT
                            RE: Dignitary Protection
                            April 28-29,2000


You are hereby assigned to assist with EOD support to the U.S. Secret Service in regard
to Vice President Al Gore’s upcoming visit to Albuquerque. You are to report to
Sergeant Doty at the District 05/Albuquerque office at 12:00 Noon on Friday, April 28,
2000.

You are to bring all assigned equipment to include your portable radio with earphones.
Uniform attire is the approved BDU. Per diem is not authorized.

Sergeant Avilucea, Sergeant Soland, and Officer Zajicek will be released for return to
their respective districts at the close of exercise on Friday, April 28, 2000. Sergeant
Doty and Officer Davies will remain on duty for Saturday, April 29, 2000, until the
Vice President departs the Albuquerque International Airport.

I am confident that you will represent the New Mexico State Police, Department of
Public Safety, in a most exemplary manner. If, for some unknown reason, you are
unable to comply with this assignment, please notify Major Forrest Smith at 827-9102
as soon as possible.

 SUBJECT: EOD TEAM IN-SERVICE SCHOOL MARCH 6-10,2000

Each of you are assigned to an EOD Team In-Service School, Albuquerque, NM from March 6-10,
2000. You will report to Sgt Doty at the Albuquerque District 5 office at 0800 hours on March 6,
2000. Training will conclude at 1400 hours on March 10 for return to your district.

Per-Diem is authorized for Lt Conticelli, Officers Davis, Standridge, Soland and Zajicek. Please use
cost center 0421800.

Personnel are to bring all assigned team equipment for this training. Each certified technician will
bring one IED (inert) for training purposes. Each certified technician may purchase items necessary
to construct the IED from Radio Shack. Provide Sgt Doty with receipts for reimbursement of these
expenses. Itinerary for the training session will be sent at a later date. BDU uniforms will be worn
throughout this training period.

Major Francis, Sgt Doty and Officer Davies will be instructing courses during this training session
and will be required to bring their lesson plans.

Please contact Officer Davies for motel reservations.

SUBJECT:       PROMOTION AND TRANSFER


CONGRATULATIONS! Effective January 24, 1998, you are hereby promoted to the rank of
Sergeant. You are transferred from the West Zone Uniform Bureau, District 6, Gallup, to the East
Zone Uniform Bureau, District 13, Raton. You will be under the management of Major Michael
J. Francis and Captain Linda Wrasman and the direct supervision of Lieutenant W. C. Wilson. You
are to report to Lieutenant Wilson in Raton for briefing and orientation, no later than 8:00 a.m. on
Monday, January 26, 1998.

In accordance with DPS Policy OPR:09:00, you will reside within your assigned station as
prescribed in this policy.

Your salary compensation will be established in accordance with DPS Policy PRS: 16:00.

Permission to travel to your newly assigned duty station in your State Police vehicle accompanied
by your family for the purpose of locating suitable housing accommodations or trailer space, is
granted. You are allowed five (5) moving days to locate and secure suitable housing or space for a
mobile home. You will receive $500.00 stipend pay to offset expenses incurred during this move.
No per diem is authorized.

You are to contact Captain Steve Herrera to make the necessary arrangements for the transportation
of your household goods or moving of your mobile home. Please refer to DPS Policy ADM:27:00,
Policies Governing Personnel Relocation Expenses, for guidelines of Department/Employee
responsibilities. Additionally, you are to make arrangements with the Office of the Chief to make
arrangements for issuance of a wallet commission as soon after January 26, 1997, as possible.

You are to contact Ms. Evangeline Clokey at the ASD Finance Bureau (827-9013) to make
arrangements to change your W-9 Form in order to have your checks sent to your new duty station.

                  INTRA-DEPARTMENTAL CORRESPONDENCE


              DATE:   January 5, 1995

              FROM:   Acting Chief Frank Tayl

                TO:   Officer Richard C. Doty
                      DPS/NM State Police
                      P. O. Box 167
                      Rehoboth, NM 87322

           SUBJECT:   Supplemental Employment


Pursuant  to   your  correspondence  dated   December 12, 1994,
permission is granted for you to obtain supplemental employment
at the University of New Mexico, Criminal Justice Department,
Gallup Campus, Gallup, New Mexico, teaching law enforcement
related subjects during your off-duty hours.

In approving your request, I wish to make it perfectly clear that
your supplemental employment shall in no way interfere with your
duties and responsibilities as an employee of the New Mexico
Department of Public Safety, State Police Division.

Furthermore, I wish at this time to bring to your attention
matters concerning our insurance coverage for accidents or
sickness incurred by employees performing duties other than State
assigned.

1.   Group insurance carriers ordinarily exclude medical expenses
     arising from injuries or sickness occurring in the course of
     any other employment or self-employment.   Therefore, you are
     advised to verify that your health insurance coverage is
     sufficient to cover yourself for injuries or illness you may
     sustain while in the course of your supplemental employment.
     Accidental death or life insurance benefits offered by State
     group health plans may similarly be affected.  Please consult
Officer Richard C.    ty
January 5, 1995
Page 2


     with the Department   of   Public   Safety Personnel   Office   for
     further details.

2.   Under the State of New Mexico’s Workmen’s Compensation
     Program, you are covered only when an accidental injury is
     sustained arising out of and in the course of your employment
     with the Department of Public Safety, State Police Division
     and any occurring disability is a natural and direct result
     of the accident.  Therefore, the accident or sickness is not
     covered if it is sustained in the course of an occupation
     other than State Police assigned duties.

3.   The same would apply to duty-related retirement benefits if
     you become totally disabled while engaged in a non-State
     Police occupation.

4.   Other benefits afforded you as an employee of the New Mexico
     Department of Public Safety, State Police Division may be
     affected and it is incumbent upon you to make specific
     inquiries if there are any other benefits that may be
     affected about which you are concerned.

Good luck with your supplemental employment.

FT:kd

cc: Major Willard Morrow
    Captain Michael J. Francis

                      INTRA-DEPARTMENTAL CORRESPONDENCE


SUBJECT:   EXPLOSIVE ORDNANCE                                  DATE:   May 10, 1991
           DISPOSAL TEAM


FROM:      CHIEF JOHN DENKO                             ATTENTION OF

TO:        OFFICER RICHARD C. DOTY                      Deputy Chief R. L. Gonzales
           DPS - State Police Division                  Major Mike Montoya
           P. O. Box 517                                Major W. D. Morrow
           Grants, New Mexico 87020                     Captain John McAninch
                                                        Captain Roger Payne


           The selections for the Explosive Ordnance Disposal Team have been made.
           Final selections were not easy due to the number of qualified candidates who
           applied.    Although, you were not selected at this time, I appreciate your
           interest in E.O.D.

           In setting the selection guidelines, the department used those mandated by
           the FBI for acceptance to the Hazardous Device School. These guidelines
           were the major factor in the majority being passed over. These guidelines
           state that the candidate must have five years on the department and five years
           retainability with the department to be eligible for school. Captain Payne
           called the Director of the Bomb Data Center to ask for a variance to these
           guidelines. After speaking with him, it was determined to adhere to the
           guidelines imposed. Other factors that received consideration on top of those
           already stated were duty station and other specialty team commitments.

           To your credit, all the candidates who applied were the best in the history of
           this department. Your application will be kept on file with the understanding
           that you will be considered for future positions in the E.O.D.

           JD :WDM:nmr

SUBJECT:                                       DATE:    February 22, 1991

FROM:


TO:          Officer Richard Doty
                                                       ATTENTION OF:
                                                       D/C Robert Gonzales
                                                       D/C A.P. Wickard
                                                       Major Mike Montoya
                                                       Capt John McAninch
                                                       Mary Ann Walz
                                                       DPS Training Bureau


You are assigned to attend "Hazardous Materials Personnel Safety" to be
held March 11-13, 1991 in Socorro, New Mexico at the State Firefighters
Training Academy. The course will begin at 10:00 a.m. on Monday and will
conclude at noon on Wednesday.

Per diem will be authorized for all officers living outside of Socorro.
Officers who must travel in excess of 100 miles are authorized to travel
to Socorro on Sunday.   You will need to arrange motel accomodations as
there are no dorms at the academy.

The class will require the use of self contained breathing apparatus and
other personal protective equipment. Attire for class attendance will be
casual clothing or fatigues.

SCBA units issued to district/subdist'rict offices or the Drug Lab Team
should be brought to the class. All Officers who have WIPP kits should
bring them.

Questions    about   the   class   should be   directed   to   Mary   Ann   Walz   at
827-9226.

SUBJECT   APPOINTMENT - EMERGENCY RESPONSE OFFICER     DATE   July 24, 1990


FROM      CHIEF NEIL W. CURRAN

TO        OFFICER RICHARD C. DOTY             ATTENTION OF
          New Mexico State Police             Lt Col Jimmy Allison
          P.O. Box 517                        Lt Col Mike Montoya
          Grants, New Mexico 87020            Captain John McAninch
                                              Captain Mark Radosevich
                                              Mary Ann Walz
                                              Headquarters Radid-


          In accordance with a request from your District Commander,
          you are appointed to the position of Emergency Response.
          Officer (ERO) for New Mexico’s hazardous materials
          emergency response (HMER) program.

          By copy of this correspondence Ms. Mary Ann Walz will be
          notified of the action taken by this office.  If she has
          not already done so, Ms. Walz will provide you with
          information regarding your responsibilities as an ERO.

          You should familiarize yourself with the emergency
          response agencies and personnel in your area to assist you
          in coordinating actions during hazardous material
          accidents and incidents.  Contacts should be made with
          local fire departments, law enforcementagencies,
          emergency medical services, civil defense, highway
          department, environmental department, local emergency
          planning committees (under SARA Title III), etc.

          In accordance with the State Police policy on appointments
          of EROs dated November 8, 1989, you must submit
          documentation of meeting Level I requirements for
          hazardous materials training to Ms. Walz prior to
          responding to any haz mat accident. Additionally, to the
          extent reasonably possible, you should be accompanied by
          an experienced ERO on your first three assignments to haz
          mat accidents.

          I congratulate you on this appointment to a very important
          position and feel confident that you will perform the
          duties of an Emergency Response Officer in an exemplary
          manner.

CONGRATULATIONS! Effective January 24, 1998, you are hereby promoted to the rank of
Sergeant You are transferred from the West Zone Uniform Bureau, District 6, Gallup, to the East
Zone Uniform Bureau, District 13, Raton. You will be under the management of Major Michael

by your family for the purpose of locating suitable housing accommodations or trailer space, is
granted. You are allowed five (5) moving days to locate and secure suitable housing or space for a
mobile home. You will receive $500.00 stipend pay to offset expenses incurred during this move.
No per diem is authorized.

of your household goods or moving of your mobile home. Please refer to DPS Policy ADM:27:00,
Policies Governing Personnel Relocation Expenses, for guidelines of Department/Employee
responsibilities. Additionally, you are to make arrangements with the Office of the Chief to make
arrangements for issuance of a wallet commission as soon after January 26, 1997, as possible.

                       INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE EMPLOYER CERTIFICATION

PERA will provide a list of individuals who have applied for a monthly annuity prior to their effective date
of retirement. Retirement and warrant processing cannot continue for any applicant whose
Employer Certifications is not received by PERA.Carefully follow ail the instructions below.

Upon completion of the certification, return the certification to PERA to ensure timely processing:
PERA Member Services
                                                          P.O.Box 2123
                                                          Santa Fe, NM 87504-2123
                                                          (505)476-9300 * (800)342-3422 * FAX (505) 476-9401
Please direct any questions concerning the Employer Certification to PERA Member Services at the
address and telephone number(s) above and photocopy the certification if additional copies are needed.

SECTION I - PERA will provide the name and social security number of the member applying for an
annuity.

SECTION II - Certify the member's termination date the statement of Hours, Earnings and Contributions
by signing in the designated area, and be sure to include title, date and telephone number. Staff members
that are authorized to verify payroll information must sign the certification.

SECTION III - Statements of Hours, Earnings and Contributions

This section must be completed for the entire last month of the member's employment, unless otherwise
specified.
        DATE: Enter the beginning and end date for which hours, wages and contributions are reported.

       HOURS: Enter the hours paid for the respective dates reported.

      GROSS WAGES: Enter the gross wages paid to the member, which are subject to PERA
      contributions for the respective dates reported. Do not include lump sum payments for unused
      annual or sick leave or other exempt payments as defined in NMSA 1978,Section 10-11-2(u)
      (1995) and PERA Rule 2.80,100.7{N) NMAC.

      MEMBER CONTRIBUTIONS :              Enter only PERA member contributions for the gross wages
      reported.
      MONTH TOTALS: Add up the hours, gross wages, and member contributions for the month and
      enter the totals on the designated lines.

      This must equal payments remitted and the amounts reported to PERA on the member's behalf.

      MONTHLY SALARY: Enter the monthly salary the member was earning upon termination.

      HOURLY SALARY: Enter the hourly salary the member was earning upon termination.

SECTION IV- Complete this section if the member is currently on leave with out pay, injury time or
      worker's compensation, PERA will indicate when this information must be provided.

                                             DETRIMENT OF PUBLIC SAF™Y
                                   Declaration for the Cash Conversion of Unused Sick Leave

NMSA 1978, Chapter 10-7-10, An employee of the state who has accumulated 600 hours of unused sick leave shall be
entitled to be paid for additional inused sick leave at a rate equal to 50% of his hourly wage multiplied by the number of
hours of unused sick leave over 600 hours not to exceed 120 hours of such sick leave in any one fiscal year. Payments are
as follows:


     A.       The amount of unused sick leave you may convert into cash in any fiscal year (July 1 through June 30) may not
              exceed 120 hours.


     B.       Payment of unused sick leave shall only be made on the payday immediately following the first full pay period in
              January and July.


     C.       Employees must declare the amounts of unused sick leave, if any, they wish to convert into cash, and the
              time(July or January), they wish to receive payment.

                               DecBaration for the Cash Conversion of Unused Sick Leave

NMSA 1978, Chapter 10-7-10, An employee of the state who has accumulated 600 hours of unused sick leave shall be
entitled to be paid for additional inused sick leave at a rate equal to 50% of his hourly wage multiplied by the number of
hours of unused sick leave over 600 hours not to exceed 120 hours of such sick leave in any one fiscal year. Payments are
as follows:


    A.        The amount of unused sick leave you may convert into cash in any fiscal year (July 1 through June 30) may not
              exceed 120 hours.


    B.        Payment of unused sick leave shall only be made on the payday immediately following the first full pay period in
              January and July.


    C.        Employees must declare the amounts of unused sick leave, if any, they wish to convert into cash, and the
              time(July or January), they wish to receive payment.


                                         Please complete ONLY the purple sections of the form

                                                 DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY
                                       Declaration for the Cash Conversion of Unused Sick Leave

      Chapter 150, Laws of 1983 and Chapter 6, Laws of 1984, entitles you to convert your unused sick leave, subject to the maximum
      provisions specified in each section of the Act, in excess of 600 hours into CASH at the rate of 50% of your hourly rate. The
      following limitations and provisions apply:

      A.       The amount of unused sick leave you may convert into cash in any one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30)) may not
               exceed 120 hours unless you arc retiring. This is in accordance to the provision set forth in Section I of the Act, Those
               retiring within the fiscal year may convert up to a maximum of 400 hours additional unused sick leave which is in
               excess of 600 hours as set forth in Section 2 of the Act.

     B.        Payment of unused sick leave shall only be made on the payday immediately following the first full pay period in
               January and July except for retirement. Individuals retiring will be paid immediately prior to retirement,

     C.        Employees must declare the amounts of unused sick leave, if any, they wish to convert into cash, and the time (July or
               January), they wish to receive payment.

                                    Declaration for the Cash Conversion of Unused Sick Leave

Chapter 150, Laws of 1983 and Chapter 6, Laws of 1984, entitles you to convert your unused sick leave, subject to the maximum
provisions specified in each section of the Act, in excess of 600 hours into CASH at the rate of 50% of your hourly rate. The
 following limitations and provisions apply:

A.        The amount of unused sick leave you may convert into cash in any one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30)) may not
          exceed 120 horn s unless you are retiring. This is in accordance to the provision set forth in Section I of the Act. Those
          retiring within the fiscal year may convert up to a maximum of 400 horns additional unused sick leave which is in
          excess of 600 hours as set forth in Section 2 of the Act.    .

B.        Payment of unused sick leave shall only be made on the payday immediately following the first full pay period in
          January and July except for retirement. Individuals retiring will be paid immediately prior to retirement.

C.        Employees must declar e the amounts of unused sick leave, if any, they wish to convert into cash, and tire time (July or
          January), they wish to receive payment.

      maximum provisions specified in each section of the Act, in excess of 600 hours into CASH at the rate of 50% of your
      hourly rate. The following limitations and provisions apply:

      A.          The amount of unused sick leave you may convert into cash in any one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30)) may
                  not exceed 120 hours unless you are retiring. This is in accordance to the provision set forth in Section I of the
                  Act. Those retiring within (he fiscal year may convert up to a maximum of 400 hours additional unused sick leave
                  which is in excess of 600 hours as set forth in Section 2 of the Act.

      B.         . Payment of unused sick leave shall only be made on the payday immediately following the first full pay period in
                  January and July except for retirement. Individuals retiring will be paid immediately prior to retirement.

      C.         Employees must declare the amounts of unused sick leave, if any, they wish to convert into cash, and the time
                 (July or January), they wish to receive payment.

                                   Declaration for the Cash Conversion of Unused Sick Leave
 Chapter 150, Laws of 1983 and Chapter 6, Laws of 1984, entitles you to convert your unused sick leave, subject to the maximum
 provisions specified in each section of the Act, in excess of 600 hours into CASH at the rate of 50% of your hourly rate. The
 following limitations and provisions apply:

 A.        The amount of unused sick leave you may convert into cash in any one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30)) may not
           exceed 120 hours unless you are retiring. This is in accordance to the provision set forth in Section I of the Act. Those
           retiring within the fiscal year may convert up to a maximum of400 hours additional unused sick leave which is in
           excess of 600 hours as set forth in Section 2 of the Act.

 B.        Payment of unused sick leave shall only be made on the payday immediately following the first full pay period in
           January and July except for retirement. Individuals retiring will be paid immediately prior to retirement.

 C.        Employees must declare the amounts of unused sick leave, if any, they wish to convert into cash, and the time (July or
           January), they wish to receive payment.

       DATE:      OCTOBER 20, 2006             .
      FROM:       CHIEF FARON W. SEGOTTA^


            TO:   SERGEANT RICHARD C. DOTY         ,

  SUBJECT:        REPRIMAND


1 am in receipt of Administrative Investigation No. 06-050-A2-06 concerning the allegation of
failure to perform supervisory duties. The allegation is sustained.       I agree with that
determination and, based upon the investigation, find that you have violated 10.5.100.8
NMAC Standard of Conduct, which states as follows:


10,5.100.8 NMAC STANDARD OF CONDUCT

B.     Employees shall satisfactorily perform their duties and assume the responsibilities of
their positions. Unsatisfactory performance may be demonstrated by violating any one of the
following provisions:


      (3)     the failure to conform to work standards established to the employees rank,
              grade or position as set forth in the specifications.


On January 27, 2006, you were working a Children, Youth and Families Department
Underage Enforcement Operation in Gallup, New Mexico.               During the operation
                      inhcon/oH a suspect holding money in his hand while being questioned.
Officer Martin took the money and placed it on top of the suspect’s vehicle trunk while he
patted him down for weapons. Officer^JJ^fbund additional money in the suspect’s pocket,
which he placed with the other money. That money was later taken by Officer
         who decided to secure i^due to inclement weather. Officer 4MMF counted the
money out to Officer              OMMk who put the money in a penalty assessment
envelope and placed it in the unmarked unit she was riding in. Also seized and secured were
narcotics. The money, approximately $130.00, later turned up missing and was never
located.

You overheard Officer^BOfcBH request SergeantMWR* to respond to the scene and,
since you were in close proximity, went to the location and took on the responsibilities of a
LETTER OF REPRIMAND
RE: SERGEANT RICHARD C. DOTY
OPSIA CASE NO. 06-050-A2-06
OCTOBER 20, 2006
PAGE 2

supervisor. Officer          asked if you couid assist in locating a vehicle involved in a drug
deal, which you agreed to do. You left to look for the vehicle, but were unsuccessful. You
then returned to the scene and again assumed the responsibilities of a supervisor, including
being briefed by Officer ^MjBfrabout what had occurred and why a supervisor was needed.
However, when Sergeant OMRf arrived, you failed to communicate with him and left shortly
thereafter. You also failed to communicate fully with the officers on scene to establish what
had occurred, what needed to be done, and what evidence had been seized. You did not
attempt to retrieve information while at the scene to ensure that the officers were acting
according to policy and that all evidence was properly handled. You also failed to ensure the
offices were complying with the recording policy while in contact with the subjects, even
though you were aware Sergeant             had specifically told the officers to ensure they had
their recording equipment with them during the earlier briefing.

Sergeant Doty, you responded to the scene, but did not request detailed information from the
officers so ensure you were fully aware of what the scene entailed. You failed to provide
supervisory oversight to ensure proper scene management and compliance with policy, and
you claimed Sergeant OMR or someone else, was in charge. Such actions show a lack of
initiative and an unwillingness to conform to work standards expected of a supervisor; you
relinquished your responsibilities as a supervisor during this incident. You were theJjrst
supervisor on scene, yet you said, “It appeared to me that Senior Patrolman BNCKMRB
was in charge of the scene.” Sergeant Doty, you are professional and expected to know
your obligations in this regard, specifically to follow Departmental rules, regulations, policies
and/or procedures and to be willing to take the extra step or ask the extra questions. Be
advised that future failures will result in significantly more severe discipline.

I trust you have learned from this incident and will henceforth perform your duties in a
competent manner and conform to Departmental policies.

December 14,1998

Dear District Commander:

On the afternoon of November 21, 1998, we were driving through Grants, New Mexico on our
way to the Grand Canyon. We had just passed Grants on 1-40 when we developed car trouble.
A German speaking Sgt., Richard Doty, stopped and helped us. He called for a mechanic, who
came out and repaired our car. Once our car was repaired we were able to continue our trip to
the Grand Canyon.

I am a citizen of the old German Democratic Republic, East Germany, but now I live in free West
Germany, in Wisbaden. This was my first trip outside of Germany. Sgt. Doty was thefirst
American policeman that I had ever met. As you could probably imagine, I was very surpised
that he was able to speak German. I can speak English, but Sgt. Doty's German was better than
my English, I am very grateful that one of your policeman was there to help me. Please give the
officer my thanks.

I enjoyed my visit to New Mexico. I spent a week in your beautiful state. I plan on visiting your
wonderful state again next year.

Thank you for having such well-prepared police officers who are able to help people in time of
need.

As I am unable to write in English, I will type this letter on my state of the art computer in
German and hope tliat you are able to find someone who is able to translate it.

Yours very sincerely,


Hans Schmidt
24 Schiersteiner Street
Wiesbaden, Germany 6200


TRANSLATOR NOTE: Mr. Schmidt makes reference to being bom in East Germany and then
moving to West Germany. He must have lived in the East for some time as he refers to his new
home as being in the "Free West". You must remember that the East German State Police,
STASI, had absolute power and people lived in fear and dread of their lives. What a relief and a
wonderful experence these people had when Officer Doty assisted them, and even more
wonderful, he could speak their language.

Thank you for the opportunity to translate this letter and also add my thanks for the fine job you
do on our highways.

Respectfully,


Warren Brashear
German Teacher
Gallup High School

July 12, 1998


New Mexico State Police                      New Mexico State Police
137 Historical Highway 66                    901 W. Highway 66
Gallup, New Mexico 87301                     Grants, New Mexico 87020


We appreciate the help received from your officers, one off-duty and one on-duty.

Sunday afternoon, June 14, we were driving west on 1-40 about 12 miles west of Grants when
we had the misfortune to puncture a tire when we ran over pieces of a truck tire that was
thrown ahead of us. We got the jack out of the trunk and were trying to read the instructions
when an off-duty officer from Gallup named Rick, I believe, came to our assistance. Rick was
with his wife on his way to Albuquerque on personal business. He removed the flat and put on
the 'donut’ which was also flat. (We really felt stupid on that!) But, Rick was not disturbed. He
called to the officer on duty in Grants. Rick then drove me and my flats to Grants and turned me
over to the officer in Grants, who returned me and my aired-up 'donut’ to my wife and my car.
The Grants’ officer put the 'donut’ on for me. We then were able to return to Grants, buy a tire,
and head for home.

Without the help of your considerate officers, we would have be stranded for a long time. During
the approximately 45 minutes that my wife waited in the car, not one of drivers of the hundreds
of vehicles that passed made any effort to help.

We will help another person when we get a chance.

And, we wish Rick and his wife success with their personal business they were attending to in
Albuquerque.

God bless you all.


Mr & Mrs John Blaylock

     greater.


     Again - thank you.


     Ann M. Parker, Safety Officer

           ■ SEPICH, A LIFE LONG RESIDENT OF RATON, NEW MEXICO, WAS BRUTALLY
             MURDERED. LAURA SEPICH WAS A LOVING MOTHER AND A HIGHLY RESPECTED
             MEMBER OF OUR LOCAL COMMUNITY.

                 WHEN MY WIFE (LAURA’S SISTER) NOTIFIED ME OF LAURA’S
           DISAPPEARANCE IN THE MORNING HOURS OF JANUARY 30™, MY WIFE AND I
           WERE AWARE OF PREVAILING CIRCUMSTANCES THAT EXISTED AND
           WARRANTED THAT THAT NORMAL MISSING PERSONS PROTOCOL WOULD NOT

           NEGOTIATION, AND EVENTUAL CAPTURE OF AN ALLEGED SUSPECT. HAD IT NOT
           BEEN FOR LT. WILSON'S EFFORTS, THE SUSPECT MAY NOT HAVE BEEN
           APPREHENDED, NOR THE BODY FOUND IN THE EXPEDIENT MANNER IN WHICH
           THIS CASE UNFOLDED. LT. WILSON’S ACTIONS IN REGARD TO THIS INCIDENT
           WERE, TO SAY THE LEAST, ABOVE AND BEYOND THE CALL OF DUTY. I CANNOT

           CHUCK WILSON AND THE OTHER GREAT OFFICERS AND PERSONNEL OF THE NEW
           MEXICO STATE POLICE.

           PERSONNEL INCLUDED IN THE INVESTIGATION, SEARCH, AND ARREST OF THE

           OUR UTMOST GRATITUDE TO THESE PEOPLE FOR BEING SUPERIOR STATE

           OUR GRIEF. GOD BLESS THE NEW MEXICO STATE POLICE, THEIR COURAGE AND
           DEDICATION TO DUTY WILL NEVER BE FORGOTTEN BY THIS FAMILY.

               DEPUTY CHIEF WILLARD D/MORROW

               TO: CHIEF FRANK R, TAYLOR

         SUBJECT: NOMINATION OF OFFICER RICHARD C, DOTY - OFFICER OF THE YEAR


      “The law enforcement officer shall regard the discharge of his duties as a public, trust and
      recognize his responsibility as a public servant. By diligent study and sincere attention
      to self-improvement he shall strive to make the best possible application of science to the
      solution of crime and, in the field of human relationships, strive for effective leadership
      and public influence in matters affecting public safety, He shall appreciate the
      importance and responsibility of his office, hold police work to be an honorable
      profession rendering valuable service to his community and his country.”

      This statement from the Law Enforcement Cannon of Ethics, written by the
      International Association of Chiefs of Police describes the dedication to duty and
      service the community displayed by Officer Richard C. Doty,

      The New Mexico State Police, officer of the year should be an individual who displays
      these qualities on a daily basis, not someone who is recognized for one or two
      outstanding deeds. Richard C. Doty Is the man. He is a seven-year veteran of the New
      Mexico State Police. He joined the department in 1988 after leaving the military.
      Officer Doty was originally stationed in Grants, New Mexico and in 1993 he transferred
      to Gallup, New Mexico,

      Officer Doty is constantly one of the top officers in District Six for overall activity. He
      spreads bls activity out and docs not work just one type of activity.
dENT BY:DPS/SPD/GALLUP/D-6     i 2~i5“96 I 15JQ9    J     NNSP District 6-*        CHIEF'S OFFICE?# 5
 <    IDC/Doty
      02-14-96
      Pg. 2

      Besides his regular duties, Officer Doty serves as a hazardous material emergency
      response officer, district range master, coach officer, district recruiter, and is a member
      of the Explosive Ordinance Disposal Team. He is proficient in all these disciplines and
      despite the time and training required to maintain his proficiency does not neglect his
      regular duties.

      Officer Doty has clearly demonstrated his leadership skills on numerous occasions while
      serving as an emergency response officer. He takes charge and is able to coordinate multi
      agency responses with ease. He is well liked and respected by the members of other law
      enforcement and fire departments and they value his advice.

      Officer Doty is willing to accept any assignment and consistently goes beyond what is
      expected of him to get the job done. He gives safety talks and lectures and is often
      requested by name to speak to community groups and alcohol prevention programs.

      Officer Doty voluntarily works the community DWI programs and the Blitzes. He does
      not just go out and collect overtime, he works hard to make a dent in the problem.
      When a sensitive investigation or difficult assignment comes up, Rick is the first person
      who comes to mind, as his supervisors know he will get the job done and do it right.
      His peers look up to him and the other officers ask his advise on handling situations or
      solving problems.

      Officer Doty is active in the community and is well known, liked and respected by the
      citizens he serves. He is involved with the schools, youth athletic programs and square
      dancing.

      Officer Richard C. Doty shows up to work every day with a smile on his face and a shine
      on his boots. He is always willing to take the extra step to get a job done and never
      refuses or shirks responsibility. He works hard, sometimes at his own expense, to better
      himself in order to be the best at his job. He truly exemplifies what a New Mexico State
      Police Officer should be and because of these reasons deserves to be officer of the year.

District Commander

Sir:

We would like to express our appreciation for the assistance
and courtesy shown to us by your office and particularly by
Officer Richard Doty.

On Thursday, February 18, 1993, we were just leaving Gallup
on our way home from Las Vegas when one of our travel trailer
wheels caught fire.  Fortunately we were able to extinguish the
blaze without damage to the trailer itself but the wheel that
was on fire needed repair before we could continue our trip
so we were stranded on the highway.  Another fortunate fact
was that the New Mexico State Police office was within
walking distance.

First, your dispatcher and another young lady in your office
(sorry - we didn't get their names} were kind enough to call
road assistance for us from Gallup.  About the same time Officer
Doty radioed in and asked if I was in the office (he had seen
our rig stopped on the highway).  He then picked me up at your
office (apologizing for having to put me in the back seat -
regulations!) and gave me a ride back to our rig because he
didn't feel it was safe for me to cross the busy 4-lane
highway again.  Officer Doty then stayed with us until help
arrived and he was sure that we would be taken care of.

We sincerely appreciate the help and concern shown by Officer
Doty and the staff in your office - it is certainly a good
reflection of the attitudes and training of the New Mexico
State Police.


                                          Stevenson

Rt. 1 - Box 256
Gordonville. TX   76245

P.S.   - Officer Doty - we did make it home without further
         trouble.  Thanks.

 TO THE EDITOR OF:      CIBOLA COUNTY BEACON
                          300 N. 2nd St.
                          Grants, N.M. 87020


 October 13,   1992

 Dear Sirs:

 In the early morning hours of Saturday, October 3, 1992 we were traveling
 to Las Vegas on vacation.  Somewhere between Albuquerque and Grants we
 began having car troubles.  We finally made it to your city (Grants, N.M.)
 Being a State Trooper in Texas, I called the state police and Trooper Rick
 Doty came to assist.  He inturn called Mr. Harry Garcia and he came to our
 location and advised that he would check out our car when he opened at 9:a.m.

 Mr. Garcia checked our car and referred us to the Chevrolet dealer just
 across the street., no charge for this by Mr. Garcia.

 At the Chevrolet dealer (Hanosh Motor Co.) we were greeted by Jimmy James.
 He immediately diagnosed our problem and replaced the part.  We were back
 on our way and vacation by noon on Saturday.

My work as a Texas State Trooper often deals with travelers that have had
vehicle problems and 1 have always attempted to assist and get them back
on the road and as efficiently and economically as possible.   This is the
first real problems with a automobile that we have experienced while
traveling or on vacation and this problem was greatly reduced by the people
that i have named above.  I would like to express my sincere appreciation
to those in your city that assisted us during this difficulty.   We felt that
we were treated fairly and justly during our difficult time.   It takes people
of this caliber to make a good town or city and you certainly have some of
those in yours,

Again, I would like to. say publicly- THANK YOU ALL -- for the assistance
and kind treatment.


                  /James (Frank) Crossley
                    306 Sagebrush
                    Waxahachie, Texas 75165

      Cibola County Highway Patrol

Chief John Denko

Narcotics Bureau

Dear Chief Denko:

The Inter Agency Narcotics Task Force and United States Customs were
investigating a drug operation on Tuesday, November 3, 1992, in the Grants area.
The investigation required assistance from your uniform division. Officers Mike
Britton, Rick Doty and David Baca assisted in this investigation.            The
investigation resulted in the seizure of 116 pounds of marijuana, seizure of
three vehicles, and one arrest.

Your officers were extremely helpful and acted in a professional manner
throughout the investigation. These officers represented your department in a
highly professional manner.

This department appreciates the assistance provided, and if we can be of any
assistance in the future, please feel free to contact us.

Sincerely,

GRANTS POLICE DEPARTMENT

Dear Chief Denko:

Last week I had some eye tissue that had to get to Gallup for
surgery.  It did not arrive in Albuquerque until late in the
evening and surgery was scheduled for 7:00 am the next day.
This tissue was came in from out of state.  With the help of
the dispatcher Victor Vigil and patrolmen Wiley Isom (Albuq.)
Rick Doty and Leonard Frietze ( Gallup/Grants) the tissue did
arrive in Gallup in time to avoid surgery delay.

After the surgery Dr. Schaffer called and thanked us for the
tissue and also asked that his appreciation be given to all
those who were involved in getting the tissue to the
hospital.  Without the help of you and your officers, this
surgery might not have been possible.  Again, we thank you
for your continued help and support.

Sincerely,


Kaye Blake
Eye Bank Technician

MEMORANDUM

    DATE:    July 19, 1989

       TO:   OFFICER RICHARD C. DOTY, DISTRICT 06 (GRANTS)

    FROM:    CHIEF NEIL W. CURRAN

 SUBJECT:    COMPLIMENTARY LETTER
             RE: CERTIFICATE - HAZARDOUS MATERIALS SAFETY BOARD


Congratulations! Enclosed please find your original certificate, dated June 14,
1989, from the Hazardous Materials Safety Board for successfully completing the
requirements for Level I certification, in compliance with provisions of the
Emergency Management Act.    Also enclosed is a copy of correspondence from
Mark A. Radosevich, Chairman of the Hazardous Materials Safety Board.

A copy of this certificate and related correspondence will be placed in your
personnel file for future reference.

Dear Chief Curran:

Enclosed please find the original certificate issued by the Hazardous
Materials Safety Board to the above captioned individual in compliance with
provisions of the Emergency Management Act.

This certificate is issued based upon submittal of the required documents,
subsequent acceptance and approval by the safety board, that this individual
has met the requirements of the above specified level established by the
safety board.

If the safety board may be of assistance to you or your department, please do
not hesitate to contact me.

Mark A. Radosevich

              July 03, 1989


              Officer Richard C. Doty
              State Police Division
              P.O. Box 570
              Grants, New Mexico 87020

              Dear Officer Doty:

              As Chief of the New Mexico State Police, I am proud to commend you for the
              manner which you performed your duties on May 31, 1989. Specifically,  you
              administered life saving cardiopulmonary resuscitation saving the life of
              Mr. Darren Medina. As evident in the correspondence received from Captain
              Joel Darby, your quick thinking, extended effort and qualities are
              essential to a devoted New Mexico State Police officer.

          Officer Richard Doty, your attitude and willingness to serve the citizens
          of New Mexico are a positive reflection on you as an individual and the
          Department.

          Thank you for an outstanding job, I am proud of men of your caliber                       which
          represents the New Mexico State Police.

              Sincerely,


          State Police Division

           TO:   SERGEANT RICHARD DOTY
                 DPS/NEW MEXICO STATE POLICE
                 PO BOX 517 905 W US 66, MILAN
                 GRANTS NEW MEXICO 87020

    SUBJECT:      5 YEAR SAFE DRIVER AWARD


I wanted to take a moment to extend to you my sincere appreciation. The job of a police officer
is inherently dangerous. There are many things we can accomplish through training to lessen
those dangers but it takes the vigilance of each and every officer of the agency to really make it
happen. Of all the dangers that a police officer faces the one they are faced with day to day is
the operation of their assigned vehicle.

I wanted to recognize you for the safe operation of your vehicle which has been identified in
your driving record. Your safe driving protects your safety and the safety of the motoring public.
The health and well being of our employees is paramount. Thank you for your efforts in making
this happen.

It has been brought to my attention that you have at least 5 years of safe driving. Please accept
this letter and a 5 year safe driving to pin to recognize your efforts.

Thanks again!

RWS

  ASSIGNMENT:
  On September 20, 2014 at approximately 1741 hours, I New Mexico State Police Officer Leo Kent Palmer
  was notified by State Police Dispatch in Gallup, NM of a request for assistance by Cibola County Sheriff’s
  Department. Dispatch advised the request was for assistance with a domestic on State Road 547 near the
  10 milepost, i was assisting NMSP Officer Joseph Grider with a traffic stop near the 53 milepost of
  Interstate 40 westbound. Officer Grider and I made a u-turn in the median and proceeded to the location
  eastbound on Interstate 40 with our emergency equipment engaged. This crash occurred in the County of
  McKinley and State of New Mexico.

  SCENE:
  As I followed Officer Grider eastbound I observed a white Commercial Motor Vehicle (CMV) move into the
  left lane as Officer Grider’s marked State Police Unit 115, Vehicle #1, neared the CMV. I observed Vehicle
  #1 move left to avoid contact with the CMV. I observed a cloud of dust as Vehicle #1 went into the dirt
  median. I observed Vehicle #1 cross the westbound lanes, drive thru the right away fence and onto the
  frontage road which is also known as State Road 122. i called dispatch and requested assistance and
  came to a stop along the right shoulder of the westbound Janes and approached Vehicle #1 to check on                   g
  Officer Grider. I requested a supervisor and medical to the scene to check on Officer Grider. Thoreau                  m
  Fire Rescue and Ambulance arrived on scene. NMSP Sgt. Richard Doty and Officer Andrew Jorgenson                        2:
                                                                                                                         c
  arrived on scene to assist with the investigation.                                                               §     3
                                                                                                                         tn
                                                                                                                         m
                                                                                                                         7J
                                                                                                                   G)
 STATEMENTS:
 Officer Grider stated he observed a black vehicle in the left lane move in-between two CMV’s as he went           3
 to pass. Officer Grider observed the white CMV closest to him moved into his lane and he took evasive
 action by steering into the median to avoid contact with the CMV. Officer Grider stated he attempted to
 hold the vehicle straight thru the median to avoid rolling the vehicle. Officer Grider stated he was
 wearing his seatbelt at the time of the crash.

  INVESTIGATION:
 At the time of crash the weather was clear and the roadway was dry. The crash occurred on Interstate 40
 near the 56 milepost This highway is marked in accordance with the National interstate Highway System.
 Vehicle #1 was traveling eastbound in the left lane with emergency equipment engaged. Vehicle #1 was
 traveling at a speed of approximately 120 miles per hour based on review of the unit dash cam video.
 The CMV did not stop and I as unable to gather any information from the dash cam to identify the CMV.
 Evidence at the scene showed that Vehicle #1 steered left into the dirt median and went into a broadside
 skid as it crossed the median. Vehicle #1 had both passenger tires deflate as it crossed the westbound
 lanes. Vehicle #1 crossed westbound lanes and continued thru the right away fence onto the eastbound
 shoulder and lane of State Road 122 where it came to rest east of the 9 milepost of State Road 122.
 Vehicle #1 had a Coban dash camera operating at the time of the crash due to the fact the emergency
 equipment was engaged prior to the crash. The video confirmed statements and observations made by
 Officer Grider and myself.

 DIAGRAM/PHOTOGRAPHS:
 The diagram was completed by Officer Jorgenson and photos were completed by Officer Jorgenson and
 myself. The photographs and diagram of Vehicle #1 were taken prior to moving the vehicle.

INJURIES:
Officer Grider was checked by Thoreau Ambulance at the scene and declined to be transported or receive
treatment at that time. Officer Grider notified Sgt. Richard Doty at the scene that he did hit his elbow
during the crash but stated it was a minor injury and did not feel treatment was necessary. Officer Grider
completed a First Notice of injury as a precaution and submitted it to Sgt. Doty.

DAMAGES/TOWING:
Vehicle #1 had damage to the undercarriage of the vehicle, the driver side mirror and passenger side tires
were deflated. Vehicle #1 was transported to the State Police Office in Gallup, NM for further inspection
and was towed by A & A Towing.

ENFORCEMENT:
No law enforcement action has been taken at this time.

Leo Kent Palmer # 326437
Patrolman
New Mexico State Police

  Assignment: 11_______________________ .
  On’May 16j’2O13 at approximately 20:258'ffoursI wSb dispatched by Gallup State Police dispatch State Road
  53, mile marker 69 in reference to a motbj-Vehiclocrasli involving a NMSP vehicle. I proceeded toward
  the area and arrived at the location of the accident at approximately 20:41 hours.

  Scene:
  ) observed Vehicle #1 facing north on the west-side shoulder area of State Road 53. l observed Vehicle                 (Xi
  #2 further north on the west-side shoulder area of State Road 53 with vehicir clebri ijxffie travel portion
  of the roadway of south-bound State Road 53. I observed Vehicle #1 had signifitahitfroiit end damage. 1
  observed Vehicle #2 had significant damage to Its passenger side. Sergeant Richard Doty, State Police
  Supervisor was on scene. State Poiice Officer Rudy Graham assisted at the scene.

 I observed Driver #1, Driver #2 and Passengers of Vehicle #2 standing next to the roadway. I observed
 Mount Taylor Ambulance arrive at the scene at approximately 21:00 hours. I observed as ambulance
 personnel evaluated all occupants of Vehicle #2. I observed the roadway was clear and dry. I observed
 there was still daylight out and the weather was calm and clear. I observed that all passengers from
 Vehicle #2 declined medical care. Driver #1 was examined by medical personnel and found not to be
 injured.

 Statements:
 Driver #1 (William Radasa) stated he was the driver and only occupant of Vehicle #1. Driver #1 stated he

  Narrative:
  On May 16, 2014 at approximately 2019 hours, I, Officer William Radasa was patrolling
  northbound on State Road 53 at or near the 70 Mile Marker when I, observed a Red in color
  passenger car traveling ata high rate of speed southbound on State Road 53. This Officer
  engaged his emergency equipment and pulled off to the right shoulder of the northbound lane
 so I could turn around on the passenger car. As I, pulled off to the right shoulder of the
 northbound roadway I observed one vehicle behind me. I waited for vehicle to pass me on the
 roadway. After the vehicle passed me I checked my left driver side mirror again. Traffic was
 light the weather conditions were clear. I didn’t see anything coming so I entered back onto
 the northbound roadway. While I was conducting a U-turn I sideswiped another vehicle
 traveling northbound on State Road 53. I then moved the unit off to the left shoulder of the
 southbound lane. I advised dispatch of the fleet and dispatch contacted Sergeant Richard
 Doty. I made sure everyone in the other vehicle was okay. Sergeant Doty arrived on scene
 shortly after and assigned Officers Graham and Hammond to take the fleet report.

   Supervisor was on scene. State Police Officer Rudy Graham assisted at the scene.

  I observed Driver #1, Driver #2 and Passengers of Vehicle #2 standing next to the roadway. I observed
  Mount Taylor Ambulance arrive at the scene at approximately 21:00 hours. I observed as ambulance
  personnel evaluated all occupants of Vehicle #2. I observed the roadway was clear and dry. I observed
  there was still daylight out and the weather was calm and clear. I observed that all passengers from
  Vehicle #2 declined medical care. Driver #1 was examined by medical personnel and found not to be
  injured.

  was traveling north-bound on State Road 53 and on duty as a State Police Officer, running traffic radar.

  and clocked the vehicle with his Unit’s radar at a speed over the posted speed limit. Driver #1 stated he

  pulled over on the east-side shoulder of State Road 53 and turned off his emergency equipment. Driver
     stated there was another vehicle traveling south-bound on State Road 53 so he was waiting for that

   SUBJECT:      REQUEST TO REMAIN ON DAY SHIFT

I am requesting to stay on Dayshift for the following reasons.

I am a single father of three young children. My Thirteenth Judicial District Court
Order lets me have custody of my children Sunday through Thursday every
week. I have no help from anyone to watch my children for the evenings and
throughout the night. I also have to care for my elderly parents whose health is
failing especially my father.

My father has episodes where he cannot breath and this usually occurs during
the early morning hours. I am the primary care giver of my parents. My ex-wife is
not very cooperative with me and does not assist with the children except during
the court ordered periods. She will not consent to changing the court order.

1 have talked to the officers in Grants District and several of the officers do not
like working dayshift and would prefer to work a different shift. They are willing to
work my night or swing shift rotation.

I would appreciate an accommodation in this matter due to my personal
circumstances.

thought he was going to pass out. I asked him why he had the can in his mouth
and he stated, "this stuff helps rn£”. The ambulance arrived and transported
Suazo to Cibola General HospitalfThe paramedics on scene took one can of the
substance to the hospital with them for identification. Officer Santiago Grijalva
arrived and we were told to document the scene and his residence. We found
cans of Ultra Duster and one can of Dust Off behind the couch in the living room.
We found cans of Ultra Duster under the sink in the trash can and in the bath tub
which was full of water. We also found cans of Ultra Duster in the bedroom. We
documented the scene with pictures. We found approximately 36 cans.

       DATE:    JANUARY 5, 2015
      FROM:     SERGEANT RICHARD C. DOTY
      THRU:     DEPUTY CHIEF JIMMY K. GLASCOC^
                MAJOR JOSEPH D. LOVATO
                CAPTAIN MITCHELL B. MAESTAS MM
                LIEUTENANT RAMON A. TERRAZAS

          TO:   CHIEF PETE N. KASSETAS
  SUBJECT:      RETIREMENT


I will retire from the New Mexico State Police effective February 1, 2015. It has
been a dream to serve the citizens of New Mexico during the past 27 years. I
thank the New Mexico State Police for hiring me and giving me the opportunity to
live a true dream. I will miss the people and the many demands placed on me
during my career. However, I will enjoy life after my long career.

My last duty day will be January 28, 2015. I will turn in my unit and equipment at
headquarters on that date. I will take one personal leave day on January 29 and
one day of compensatory leave on January 30, 2015. My official retirement date,
per PERA, is February 1,2015.

RCD:rcd

          L         l/We have applied fur a mortgage loan. As part of the application process, the lender
                    and any investor to whom the lender may sell or consider selling my mortgage may
                    verify information contained in my/our loan application and in other documents required
                    in connection with the loan, either before the loan is closed or as part of it’s quality
                    control program.

          2.        I/We authorize you to provide the lender, and any investor to whom the lender may sell
                    or consider selling my mortgage any and all information and documentation they
                    request. Such information includes, but is not limited to, employment history and
                    income; bank, money market, and similar account balances; credit history; and copies of
                    income tax returns.

          3        I/We authorize the lender and any investor to whom the lender may sell my mortgage or
                   consider selling my mortgage to obtain a consumer report on me/us during the review of
                   my application and at any lime in the future to use in extending, modifying, or otherwise
                   reviewing my loan.

          4.        The lender or any investor that purchases the mortgage may address this authorization to
                   any party named in the loan application.

     SUBJECT:    REQUEST TO CARRY PERSONAL BACKUP WEAPON - APPROVED


I have received your request for permission to carry your personal
firearm—an AMT, Model #380, .380 caliber, automatic pistol, serial #T58645, as
a backup weapon and while off duty in lieu of your departmental issue weapon.

Your request is hereby approved on the basis that the weapon has been
inspected, found to be in good condition, and you have qualified with it
according to the Range Master at the time of qualification.
